opening.text: Walk a dark path with a lamp, and you can see the next step. You do not need to see the whole road.
The Bible is a lamp like that. People have used it for thousands of years. Let’s see why it still lights the way.

mainMessage.text: The Holy Bible is the word of God. It points us to Jesus Christ. It was given by inspiration. When we study it every day, it blesses our lives. It stands beside the Book of Mormon.

blocks.text: A lamp that does not go out.
The psalmist said God’s word lights our path. Isaiah said it lasts forever.
Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand for ever.
Elder M. Russell Ballard of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Miracle of the Holy Bible” from the April 2007 general conference.
It is a miracle that we have the Bible’s powerful doctrine, principles, poetry, and stories.
The light has reached us across the centuries.
The light points to Jesus Christ.
After the Resurrection, the Savior walked with two disciples and taught them from the scriptures. John said the Gospel was written so we would believe.
And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.
But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name.

Elder M. Russell Ballard of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Miracle of the Holy Bible” from the April 2007 general conference. He said the Bible “testifies throughout its pages of the Lord Jesus Christ.”
It testifies throughout its pages of the Lord Jesus Christ.
Follow the lamp and you find Him.
Given by inspiration.
Paul said all scripture comes from God. Peter said the prophets spoke as the Holy Ghost moved them.

All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.

Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation. For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “My Words … Never Cease” from the April 2008 general conference.
Continuing revelation does not demean or discredit existing revelation.
God spoke then, and He speaks now.
Carry the lamp every day.
The people of Berea checked the scriptures daily. Joshua was told to keep the book close and think about it day and night.
These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.

This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.
Elder M. Russell Ballard of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Miracle of the Holy Bible” from the April 2007 general conference.
Honest, diligent study of the Bible does make us better and better.
A little each day adds up.
Live on every word.
The Savior said we live on more than bread. Paul said the scriptures give us hope.
But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.
For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.
Elder M. Russell Ballard of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Miracle of the Holy Bible” from the April 2007 general conference.
We tend to love the scriptures that we spend time with.
Spend time, and the love will come.
Two books, one Savior.
God has always spoken through prophets. The Church is built on the foundation of apostles and prophets, with Jesus Christ as the cornerstone.
Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.

Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God; And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone.
Elder M. Russell Ballard of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Miracle of the Holy Bible” from the April 2007 general conference.
The Book of Mormon does not dilute nor diminish nor de-emphasize the Bible.
The two books work together.

blocks.text: Jesus grew up in Nazareth. Every Sabbath, He did something regular.
And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up: and, as his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up for to read.

story.title: The book found in the temple

blocks.text: In the days of King Josiah, the scriptures had been lost for years. Then a priest found them.
And Hilkiah the high priest said unto Shaphan the scribe, I have found the book of the law in the house of the Lord. And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.
When the king heard the words, he changed his life. The scriptures can do the same for us when we open them.

story.title: Hearts that burned

blocks.text: Two disciples walked to Emmaus. They did not know the stranger beside them was the risen Lord.
And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?
They felt it when the scriptures were opened. We can feel the same when we read and ask Him to teach us.

blocks.text: Jesus read from Isaiah in the synagogue in Nazareth. Then He told the people what it meant.
And he began to say unto them, This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.
